title.narrative: Drought Emergency Response

description.narrative:
In Oromia region, which is among the worst affected areas, where 1,553,649 people in 70 districts of seven Zones (i.e., Borena, Guji and west Guji, East and West Bale, Arsi and west Arsi), are severely af-fected and needed immediate assistance . Borena, and both Bale Zones bear the biggest burden of loss of livestock and harvest failure. As of November 30,2021, over 100,500 livestock have died in the two. zones, with the most significant losses in Borena. The current emergency put further pressure on the al-ready existing multiple crises because of the desert locust and previous poor rain performance. The cu-mulative effect of drought and desert locusts contributed 72% productivity loss and directly affected the lives and livelihood of 248,941 HHs in the zones. Even though the target community members have lots of needs to be addressed, with available limited resources, the consortium planned to implement the project in Madda Walabu and Arero districts where EECMY DASSC will provide food item support to Madda Walabu Woreda, Bale Zone and HUNDEE will do the same in Arero district, Borena Zone while Cordaid will manage the multi-purpose cash transfer in both Woredas. Both HUNDEE and EECMY DASSC signed operation agreement with their respective Zones and already the project implementation.
Cordaid will distribute Multipurpose cash (MPC) for 800 HH (4800 people) in both Madda Walabu and Arero districts. The beneficiaries are entitled to 2,440 ETB per household/round for two rounds. Cor-daid will supervise the cash transfer process. Post-distribution monitoring (PDM) will be conducted as soon as the distribution is completed.

The specific objective of the project is to provide a multipurpose cash for 800HH (4,000 People) for se-verely affected households resides in Hallona and Haro-Dimtu kebeles of Arero District of Borana Zone and Barisa and Hara haji kebeles of Madda Walabu District of Bale Zone.
Total: 800 HH (4800 people)  Direct Male and Female: 2,880 females and 1.920 males  Indirect Male and Female: 2,880 females and 1.920 males

title.narrative: Output KRIs - RI
CSH-R1: Number of people benefitting from unconditional and unrestricted cash transfers

description.narrative: Unconditional transfers are provided to beneficiaries without the recipient having to do anything in return in order to receive the assistance . Unrestricted transfers can be used entirely as the recipient chooses i.e. there are no restrictions on how the transfer is spent (Definitions of CALP). It can be delivered e.g. through local banks, shops, traders, local money transfer companies, remittance companies and post offices in either one or several instalments.
